sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
The path was not smooth: FY2019 operating income fell 58.9% and net income 60.0% [D97][D98], while FY2020 operating income rose 186.2% and net income 234.3% [D148][D149].

The FY2019 collapse came from an $8.3 billion asset impairment charge, including $6.8 billion of Shave Care goodwill, driven by currency devaluations, decelerating category growth and tougher competition [X112][X109][P62].
FY2020's rebound reflected $8.3 billion of that base-period charge plus higher sales and gross margin [P71].
Since FY2020 the top line has grown at 2.0% a year to FY2026 [F4][F10][D664], with FY2025 the slow year at 0.3% growth [D406].
The US was the growth engine for most of the window, contributing 4.0pp of FY2020 growth and 3.7pp in FY2022 [D518][D524], but only 0.1pp in FY2026 [D536].
In FY2026 the Non-US business contributed 3.1pp of the 3.3% revenue growth [D511][D457], with Beauty adding 1.3pp and Fabric & Home Care 0.8pp [D603][D543].
FY2026 sales rose on favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Operating income grew faster than revenue over the window, at a 4.1% CAGR against 3.3% [F202][F201], but FY2026 reversed that with operating income down 3.4% on 3.3% revenue growth [D458][D457].
Diluted EPS compounded at 1.9% against net income's 0.5% [F205][F203], helped by a diluted share count that fell from 2,740.4 million to 2,422.5 million [X115][X124].
The FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% sits just above the window median of 22.1% and well above the FY2019 low of 8.1% [F30][D648][D646].
The margin fell 1.6pp in FY2026 as gross margin dropped and marketing spending rose [D470][P25], with cost of revenue costing 1.0pp and SG&A 0.6pp [D483][D485].
Gross margin narrowed on unfavorable category mix, partly offset by lower commodity costs and productivity savings [P5].
Net margin of 18.4% trails operating margin by 4.3pp [F50][D693], and the FY2026 tax rate rose to 20.8% from 20.3% [D443][D392].
The higher tax rate came from lower excess share-based compensation benefits and unfavorable geographic mix [P23].

Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income in FY2026 [F80][D444], above the window median of 1.25x only slightly below it [D683], and free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x net income [F100][D445].
Operating cash flow rose 9.8% as net earnings plus non-cash items generated about $19.5 billion, with payables adding $919 million and inventory consuming $641 million [D462][P3].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% is near the window median of 17.2% [D441][D654], and capex at 5.1% of revenue is the highest since FY2018 [D440][D27].
Capex ran at 1.40x D&A in FY2026, the top of the window [D446], as investing outflow widened to $4.6 billion [F110][P2].

The company carries net debt of $24.2 billion, or 27.8% of revenue [D450][D451], a smaller net debt burden than the staples peer median of 32.3% of revenue and in the 67th percentile of three peers [D695][D694].
Long-term debt fell 8.6% to $22.8 billion [F190][D468], while cash rose 4.0% to $9.9 billion [F140][D466].
Buybacks and dividends of $15.3 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow [D452][D453], and the diluted share count fell 1.3% [D476].

Return on average equity of 30.1% ranks in the 33rd percentile against a peer median of 44.4% [D456][D681][D680], reflecting a thin equity base of $54.3 billion against $126.5 billion of assets [F200][F130].
The current ratio of 0.68x is below 1.0x and below the window median of 0.72x [F180][D663], a persistent feature of a negative working-capital model rather than a new stress.
Buybacks plus dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 at 116.6% and FY2026 at 100.7% [D402][D453], funded partly by debt and leaving little cushion if free cash flow dips.
Days inventory outstanding rose to 69 days from 52 in FY2017 [D455][D21], the highest in the window.
Inventory consumed $641 million of cash in FY2026 on higher safety stock and new product initiatives [P3], a working-capital drag worth watching.
If the operating margin falls below the 22.1% window median [D648], the FY2026 margin compression would look structural rather than a one-year mix effect; the FY2027 10-K will show it.
Free cash flow margin at 17.4% [D441] against the 17.2% median [D654] is the level to hold; a drop toward the 14.4% FY2017 low [D652] would pressure the 100.7% payout ratio [D453].
Days inventory outstanding at 69 days [D455] should be watched against the 63-day FY2024 level [D352]; further build would confirm the safety-stock drag cited in the FY2026 filing [P3].
